sections.content:
Population change in South Cambridgeshire in 2032

The population in South Cambridgeshire is projected to increase from 165,709 people in 2022 to 183,906 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 11,061 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in South Cambridgeshire
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In South Cambridgeshire, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 1,944, with 15,992 births and 14,048 deaths in South Cambridgeshire between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in South Cambridgeshire by 1.2%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 11,061, with 133,984 people moving to the area and 122,923 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in South Cambridgeshire by 6.7%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 685, with 3,129 people moving to the area and 3,813 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in South Cambridgeshire by 0.4%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 5,954, with 14,648 people moving to the area and 8,694 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in South Cambridgeshire by 3.6%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in South Cambridgeshire in 2032

The median age in South Cambridgeshire is projected to rise from 42 years in 2022 to 43 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 21% of the population in South Cambridgeshire are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 19% in 2022.

sections.title: The 80 to 89 age group are set to see the largest change in South Cambridgeshire between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in South Cambridgeshire is projected to stay the same, at around 62%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 304 to 309 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in South Cambridgeshire?

In 2032, 21% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 23% in 2022.

This is above average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in South Cambridgeshire between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 9% to 8%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 8%
